place_fields.summary: Chinaga Betta is a hill trek near Swandenahalli in Tumakuru district, running through Thimlapura Wildlife Sanctuary.
place_fields.best_time: July to September for lush post-monsoon scenery; October to January for drier conditions.

planning_attributes.description: A moderate trek through forest, grassland and rocky sections, with viewpoints including Bandara Betta and Kambada Kallu.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The trek starts at Torana Anjaneya Swamy Temple near Swandenahalli; the site is about 80 km from Bengaluru and accessible by road via NH 48.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Government permission/permit is required; Karnataka Eco-Tourism lists a 250 INR booking and says the trek is not for children.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Some rocky sections can be slippery in heavy rain; the final climb includes steep rock and rope-assisted sections.
planning_attributes.notes: Official Karnataka Eco-Tourism lists the trek as 5.5 km and about 4 hours, moderate difficulty.

place_fields.vibe: rocky pilgrimage hill and sunrise trek
place_fields.summary: Shivagange is a mountain peak and Hindu pilgrimage centre near Dobbaspet, known for rocky trekking terrain, temples and panoramic views.
place_fields.best_time: October to March is a commonly recommended period; early morning is preferable for trekking.

planning_attributes.description: A popular hill trek with rock-cut steps, railings on steep sections, ancient temples, sacred springs and a summit Nandi.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Known as Dakshina Kashi; the hill is shaped like a Shiva Linga and contains several historic temples. It is a protected monument site.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The hill is about 7 km from Bengaluru-Tumakuru NH 48; KSRTC buses and taxis are available. The nearest major railway stations are in Bengaluru.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The summit approach becomes steep and narrow. Monkeys are common; avoid carrying exposed food. Rain can make rocky sections slippery.
planning_attributes.notes: The Government of Karnataka describes the trail as well marked and suitable for beginners, with safety rails on steep summit sections.
